newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says plans no new finance measures now.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says plans no new finance measures now.

text.p: Thai authorities have no plans for any new finance measures in the immediate aftermath of the baht's float as the impact of the move remains unclear, a senior official said on Monday.

"We need more time to see and study the baht's direction and movement after the flotation. It's too early to implement any new measures right now," finance ministry permanent secretary Chatumongkol Sonakul told reporters.
Chatumongkol was speaking after the meeting of a panel formed by the Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya last week to study the impact of the baht's de facto devaluation.
Financial authorities last Wednesday shocked Asian markets by floating the baht, ending 13 years of pegging it to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
Chatumongkol said lack of activity in the foreign exchange market and wide quoted spreads of the baht versus the dollar made it difficult to analyse the managed float's impact.
